_: The MANAGED subset of ~/.claude/settings.json — the entries the box's mechanical gates depend on, and nothing else. Everything not named here (theme, model, effort, extra allow/ask/deny rules) belongs to whoever uses the box and is never reported as drift. cc-settings is the only reader; install.sh and cc-audit both ask it, so they agree by construction.
_proven: 2026-08-31: the UserPromptSubmit row below was canonical here for days and never applied to the live file, so the ask ledger captured nothing automatically — 27 rows were typed in by hand. The audit reported it, but as '27 lines differ', with a theme change weighing the same as a missing gate. Naming the subset is what makes the report actionable.

hooks.why: the four owner gates (merge/deploy, external comms, destructive, secrets). Unapplied, a worker session can merge, deploy and push to the default branch.
commits and pushes a track's work at the end of every turn. Unapplied, an iteration that ends leaves its changes only in the worktree.
captures every owner ask into the ledger. Unapplied, the ledger only holds what a session remembered to type in by hand.

_deny: REQUIRED deny rules — the live file may hold more (the owner's own), never fewer. cc-settings reports a missing one and REFUSES to write it: `permissions` is what decides what a session may do, so nothing automatic may edit it. See cc-settings apply.
